cards.text: Solomon is king of Israel, and he just asked God for an understanding heart to judge His people (1 Kings 3:9). Now two prostitutes come and stand before him. First case on his desk, and I bet he was hoping for a parking ticket.

cards.question: One woman speaks first. She says she and the other woman live in the same ___.

cards.text: She says she gave birth in that house. On the third day after, the other woman had a baby too.

cards.question: The first woman says someone else was staying in the house with the two of them.

cards.text: Then comes the hard part. During the night, she says, the other woman's son died.

cards.question: According to the first woman, how did the other woman's son die?

cards.text: So, she says, the other woman got up in the middle of the night while she was asleep.

cards.question: What does the first woman say the other woman did in the middle of the night?

answers.text: Swapped her dead son for the living one
Hid her dead son outside the house
Woke her up and asked for help

cards.text: The next morning she gets up to nurse her son, and he's dead. Then she takes a closer look.

cards.question: When the first woman looks closer at the dead baby, she realizes he isn't the son she gave birth to.

cards.text: Then the other woman cuts in, and friend, she is NOT having it.

cards.question: The other woman tells the king the ___ one is her son.

cards.text: So they argue right there in front of the king. Solomon says it all back: this one says her son's alive and the other's is dead, and that one says the exact opposite.

cards.question: Two stories, no witnesses. What does Solomon tell them to bring him?

cards.text: So they bring the king a sword. I bet that room got real QUIET real fast.

cards.question: Solomon orders the living child cut in two, with half going to each woman.

cards.text: Now, I know how that sounds. Stay with me, friend, and watch the two women.

cards.question: The woman whose son is alive speaks up first. What does she beg the king to do?

answers.text: Give the baby to the other woman
Let the two of them share him
Give her time to find a witness

cards.question: She speaks up because she yearned with ___ for her son.

cards.text: Then the other woman opens her mouth, and I had to read it twice. TWICE. I set my mustache down for that one.

cards.question: After the woman whose son is alive offers to give him up, what does the other woman say?

answers.text: Neither of us gets him so cut him
Let the palace raise him instead
Give us until morning to decide

cards.question: Solomon gives his ruling. Who gets the living baby?

answers.text: The woman who begged to spare him
The woman who said to cut him

cards.question: Solomon says the baby must not be killed, because the woman who begged for him is his mother.

cards.text: No witnesses. No paperwork. One sword nobody swung, and the truth came walking out all by itself.
Word travels faster than a group chat. All Israel hears about the judgment the king gave.

cards.question: When all Israel hears about the king's judgment, they stand in awe of him.
The people saw that the ___ of God was in Solomon to administer justice.

findings.problem: "First case on his desk" states as a fact that this is Solomon's first case. 1 Kings 3:16 only says "At that time." The text never says this is his first case. The parking-ticket joke can stay if it doesn't depend on that added claim.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Card 7 says the other woman got up "while she was asleep." That setup makes the wrong answer "Woke her up and asked for help" easy to rule out before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "Now, I know how that sounds. Stay with me, friend, and watch the two women." tells no part of the passage. It cites 1 Kings 3:26 but carries none of that verse's content. It is only a storyteller aside with nothing from the passage for the joke to ride on.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: "I set my mustache down for that one" doesn't land. His mustache is part of him and works as his hands, so it can't be set down. A reader would say "huh?" The line also makes the mustache the punchline.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: "No witnesses. No paperwork. One sword nobody swung, and the truth came walking out all by itself." recaps verses 24 to 27, which have already been told and asked. It doesn't move the passage forward.
